stem: A team runs `dbt clone --state prod_artifacts` on a platform that has no zero-copy cloning. They must still end up with queryable objects in the development schema for every selected model. What does dbt produce?

option_texts.A: An error, because the `clone` materialization needs platform support
option_texts.B: A pointer view that selects from the source object
option_texts.C: A full table copy, sized the same as the source relation
option_texts.D: Nothing at all, because pre-existing relations are left alone

drill_answer_short: Without zero-copy support dbt falls back to a simple pointer view
decision_hinge: If your data platform supports zero-copy cloning of tables and this model exists as a table in the source environment, dbt will create it in your target environment as a clone. Otherwise, dbt will create a simple pointer view, select star from the source object.

plausible_options.C: They must still end up with queryable objects in the development schema for every selected model

A.signal: A team runs `dbt clone --state prod_artifacts` on a platform that has no zero-copy cloning
A.requires_fact: The dbt clone command clones selected nodes from the specified state to the target schemas. This command makes use of the clone materialization.

D.signal: must still end up with queryable objects in the development schema
D.requires_fact: By default, dbt clone will not recreate pre-existing relations in the current target. To override this, use the --full-refresh flag.

distractor_traps.A: T1: the command does not fail without zero-copy support; it changes what it creates
distractor_traps.C: T3: a real copy is what zero-copy cloning avoids, and it is not the fallback either
distractor_traps.D: T5: the pre-existing-relation rule is real, but the stem describes a fresh development schema

stem: An analyst must validate a change to a mart by pointing an external BI dashboard at the modified tables before the pull request merges. The team wants the approach with the LEAST warehouse spend that still satisfies the dashboard. Which approach should they choose?

option_texts.A: Run the build with `--defer --state`, since deferral is cheaper than cloning
option_texts.B: Run `dbt clone --state`, since the dashboard needs real warehouse objects
option_texts.C: Run a full `dbt build` of the whole project into a personal warehouse schema
option_texts.D: Run `dbt compile` and hand the compiled SQL to the dashboard owner

drill_answer_short: Only clone creates real objects an external tool can query
decision_hinge: Unlike deferral, dbt clone requires some compute and creation of additional objects in your data warehouse. In many cases, deferral is a cheaper and simpler alternative to dbt clone. However, by creating actual data warehouse objects, dbt clone allows you to test out your code changes on downstream dependencies.

plausible_options.A: The team wants the approach with the LEAST warehouse spend that still satisfies the dashboard
plausible_options.C: must validate a change to a mart by pointing an external BI dashboard at the modified tables

D.signal: pointing an external BI dashboard at the modified tables before the pull request merges
D.requires_fact: dbt compile is similar to dbt run except that it doesn't materialize the model's compiled SQL into an existing table.

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — deferral redirects refs inside dbt, so no object appears for an external tool
distractor_traps.C: T7: over-engineering — it produces real objects but rebuilds the entire project to do it
distractor_traps.D: T2: compiled SQL is text, not a relation a dashboard can point at

stem: A second `dbt clone` run must replace relations that a previous clone already created in the target. Because dbt clone will not recreate pre-existing relations by default, the team needs to add the ____ flag.
decision_hinge: By default, dbt clone will not recreate pre-existing relations in the current target. To override this, use the --full-refresh flag.

stem: A CI run must build a changed model and everything downstream of it. Several downstream models also read from other parents that have never been built in this schema. The selection must therefore pull in those other parents too. Which selector does that?

option_texts.A: `--select "+my_model+"`, which adds the model's own ancestors too
option_texts.B: `--select "my_model+"`, which adds every descendant of the model
option_texts.C: `--select "@my_model"`, which adds the ancestors of the descendants
option_texts.D: `--select "my_model+1"`, which steps one edge past the model

drill_answer_short: @ is + plus all ancestors of all descendants
decision_hinge: The at operator is similar to plus, but will also include all ancestors of all descendants of the selected model. This is useful in continuous integration environments where you want to build a model and all of its descendants, but the ancestors of those descendants might not exist in the schema yet.

plausible_options.A: Several downstream models also read from other parents that have never been built in this schema

B.signal: The selection must therefore pull in those other parents too
B.requires_fact: Placed after a model or resource, the plus operator includes the resource itself and all its descendants, which are its downstream dependencies.

D.signal: A CI run must build a changed model and everything downstream of it
D.requires_fact: You can adjust the behavior of the plus operator by quantifying the number of edges to step through, so my_model+1 selects my_model and its first-degree descendants.

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling — it adds the selected model's own ancestors, not the descendants' ancestors
distractor_traps.B: T4: it covers descendants but never reaches the descendants' other parents
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — the n-plus operator limits depth rather than widening the graph

stem: A nightly job dies immediately with a warehouse permission error, before any node executes. An on-call engineer runs `dbt retry` and sees nothing execute. The engineer must get the job's nodes built tonight. What is going on, and what should they do?

option_texts.A: Retry skipped nodes that succeeded earlier, so pass `--full-refresh` as well
option_texts.B: Retry reuses stale state, so delete `target/` and run `dbt retry` again
option_texts.C: Retry found no recorded nodes, so check `run_results.json` and re-run the full job
option_texts.D: Retry treated the permission error as a warning, so add `--warn-error` and retry

drill_answer_short: With no nodes executed there is nothing to retry from — re-run the full job
decision_hinge: If no nodes are executed before the failure, for example if a run failed early due to a warehouse connection or permission errors, retry won't run anything since there are no recorded nodes to retry from. In these cases, we recommend checking your run_results.json file and manually re-running the full job so the nodes build.

plausible_options.B: An on-call engineer runs `dbt retry` and sees nothing execute

A.signal: A nightly job dies immediately with a warehouse permission error, before any node executes
A.requires_fact: If the previously executed command completed successfully, retry will finish as no operation.

D.signal: The engineer must get the job's nodes built tonight
D.requires_fact: Enabling WARN_ERROR config or setting the --warn-error flag will convert all dbt warnings into errors.

distractor_traps.A: T5: right that nothing ran, wrong cause — a full refresh does not create nodes to retry from
distractor_traps.B: T5: right that artifacts are involved, wrong direction — deleting target discards what retry reads
distractor_traps.D: T2: warn-error changes what counts as a failure; a permission error was already an error

stem: An on-call engineer must pick the right recovery tool for each situation without rebuilding more than necessary. Match each situation to the dbt capability that addresses it.
match_left: A run stopped halfway and must resume from the failure
An incremental model's schema changed and it must be rebuilt from scratch
Production tables must be copied into a development schema as real objects
A subset must run without building its unselected upstream parents
drill_answer_short: retry resumes, full-refresh rebuilds, clone copies, defer redirects
decision_hinge: Retry re-executes the last invocation from the point of failure. If you provide the --full-refresh flag to dbt run, dbt will treat incremental models as table models. The dbt clone command clones selected nodes from the specified state to the target schemas. Defer makes it possible to run a subset of models without having to first build their upstream parents.
